$comment: Habit catalog (SPEC §3.1). One entry per stable habit ID. `kinds`: check = detectable in a game, drill = trainable with puzzles, info = guidance only. `source` says how it is detected or drilled; `phase` is when the check/drill is planned. Per-level selection lives in data/levels/level-N.json. `video` links the clearest explanation in the Building Habits v2 series (episode, timestamp); summaries are our own words.

no-premoves.label: no premoves
no-premoves.source: Move time from %clk deltas: about 0.1s means a premove.
no-premoves.guidance: Think on every move. A premove skips the one look that catches a hanging piece.

premoves-under-10s.label: premoves only under 10s
premoves-under-10s.source: Move time from %clk deltas; allowed only when the clock is under 10 seconds.
premoves-under-10s.guidance: Premove only when your clock is almost out. Otherwise, look at the board first.

no-tactics.label: no tactics
no-tactics.guidance: Don't hunt for combinations yet. Develop, keep your pieces safe and take what is free.

no-gambits.label: no gambits
no-gambits.source: no-sacrifices restricted to pawns in roughly the first 12 moves.
no-gambits.guidance: Don't give away pawns in the opening for a vague attack. Keep material level and develop.

no-sacrifices.label: no sacrifices
no-sacrifices.source: Material given up and not won back within 2 plies (not a forced recapture). Stockfish separates sound sacrifices from blunders.
no-sacrifices.guidance: Don't give up material unless you can see it come back. Solid beats speculative.

never-resign.label: never resign
never-resign.source: PGN termination: the user lost by resignation.
never-resign.guidance: Play it out. Opponents at every level miss wins, stalemate and flag. Learn the basic mates so you can finish games yourself.

know-piece-moves.label: know how the pieces move
know-piece-moves.guidance: Be fluent with every piece, including castling, en passant and promotion.

center-control.label: center control
center-control.source: Score central squares occupied or attacked through the opening (soft).
center-control.guidance: Put pawns and pieces where they touch d4, e4, d5 and e5. If a piece can't go to the center, put it where it controls the center.

castle-asap.label: castle asap
castle-asap.source: Plies where castling was legal and not played; the move number when the user castled (or never).
castle-asap.guidance: Castle as soon as it is legal. A safe king makes everything else easier.

castle-quickly.label: castle quickly
castle-quickly.source: Plies where castling was legal and not played; the move number when the user castled (or never).
castle-quickly.guidance: Get the king safe early, usually within the first ten moves.

develop-aggressively.label: develop aggressively
develop-aggressively.source: Minor pieces still on their starting squares after move N; the same piece moved twice before all minors are out.
develop-aggressively.guidance: Bring every minor piece out before moving any piece twice.

always-trade.label: always trade
always-trade.source: An equal trade was available and declined (low weight; informational).
always-trade.guidance: When an even trade is on offer, take it. Fewer pieces means fewer things to blunder.

no-hanging-pieces.label: no hanging pieces
no-hanging-pieces.source: After the user's move, any user piece that loses material by static exchange evaluation. Confirmed with Stockfish.
no-hanging-pieces.guidance: Before every move, check that each of your pieces is defended or safe.

take-free-pieces.label: take free pieces
take-free-pieces.source: The opponent left material capturable with a positive static exchange and the user didn't take it. Confirmed with Stockfish.
take-free-pieces.guidance: Before every move, check whether anything of theirs can be taken for free.

rpm.label: rpms (random pawn moves)
rpm.source: Soft check, no detector yet: once the user's minor pieces are developed and the king has castled, count quiet queenside pawn moves vs aimless piece moves.
rpm.guidance: Once your pieces are developed, you've castled and there's nothing useful for them to do, push a queenside pawn instead of shuffling pieces around.

snorkel.label: snorkel (luft)
snorkel.source: After castling, h3/h6 on the castled side (g3/g6 also counts) within 5 own moves; flag it when, 6 moves after castling, the king still sits behind three unmoved pawns. Series games: 89-97% of games at every level, median 1-2 moves after castling.
snorkel.guidance: Once you've castled, push the pawn in front of your king one square (h3 or h6) so it can never be mated on the back rank.

rooks-to-middle.label: rooks to the middle
rooks-to-middle.source: First rook move after castling goes to the d- or e-file, within 9 own moves of castling; best with check while the enemy king is still in the middle. Series games: 90-96% at every level.
rooks-to-middle.guidance: After castling, bring a rook to the d- or e-file. If the enemy king is still in the middle, do it right away.

double-rooks-open-file.label: double rooks on open files
double-rooks-open-file.source: In the middlegame, both rooks on the same open or half-open file (soft).
double-rooks-open-file.guidance: When a file opens up, stack both rooks on it to take it over.

queen-up.label: queen up
queen-up.guidance: With the rook centralized, step the queen up one square to connect the rooks and make room for the second one.

queen-trade-after-sac.label: trade queens after a sacrifice
queen-trade-after-sac.guidance: If your opponent gives up a piece to attack, offer a queen trade straight away. Their attack stops and you keep the extra piece.

no-early-queen.label: no early queen
no-early-queen.guidance: Develop knights and bishops before the queen; an early queen just gets chased around.

endgame-king-activity.label: active king in the endgame
endgame-king-activity.source: In the endgame (non-pawn material under a threshold): the king's distance from the center over time, and king moves.
endgame-king-activity.guidance: Once the queens are off, march the king to the middle. It is a fighting piece.

attack-pawns.label: attack pawns
attack-pawns.source: In the endgame, moves that attack or win enemy pawns (soft).
attack-pawns.guidance: In the endgame, go after their pawns: every one you win is a potential queen.

basic-tactics.label: basic tactics
basic-tactics.source: Lichess puzzles filtered by theme and repertoire opening (pin, fork, skewer, discovery).
basic-tactics.guidance: Learn the four basic patterns: pin, fork, skewer and discovered attack.

basic-and-advanced-tactics.label: basic and advanced tactics
basic-and-advanced-tactics.source: Lichess puzzles filtered by theme and repertoire opening.
basic-and-advanced-tactics.guidance: Add deflection, attraction, clearance, interference and in-between moves to the basics.

basic-openings-and-responses.label: openings and responses
basic-openings-and-responses.source: Repertoire trainer; game review reports where the user left the repertoire.
basic-openings-and-responses.guidance: Know a set answer to each common reply, one opening per color.

active-not-reactive.label: be active, not reactive
active-not-reactive.guidance: Make your own threats instead of only answering theirs.

opposition-pawn-rook-endgames.label: opposition, pawn and rook endgames
opposition-pawn-rook-endgames.source: Hand-curated endgame positions played against Stockfish (§5.4).
opposition-pawn-rook-endgames.guidance: Know the opposition and the basic king-and-pawn and rook endings cold.

lucena-philidor-n-vs-b.label: lucena, philidor, knight vs bishop
lucena-philidor-n-vs-b.source: Hand-curated endgame positions played against Stockfish (§5.4).
lucena-philidor-n-vs-b.guidance: Win the Lucena, hold the Philidor, and know when a knight beats a bishop.

trade-when-up-not-when-down.label: trade when up, not when down
trade-when-up-not-when-down.guidance: Ahead in material, simplify. Behind, keep pieces on and look for chances.

rook-placement.label: rook placement
rook-placement.guidance: Rooks belong on open files, on the seventh rank and behind passed pawns.

all-checkmate-patterns.label: all checkmate patterns
all-checkmate-patterns.source: Lichess puzzles filtered by checkmate-pattern themes and repertoire opening.
all-checkmate-patterns.guidance: Recognize the named mates: back rank, smothered, Anastasia, Arabian, Boden and more.

pawn-structure-weak-pawns.label: pawn structure, weak pawns
pawn-structure-weak-pawns.guidance: Spot isolated, doubled and backward pawns, yours and theirs, and play against the weak ones.
